results.content: # Americans' wealth and income are up, but credit card debt is too. Americans' wealth rose from 2022 to 2025 at a far slower pace than it did during the COVID-19 pandemic years, the Federal Reserve's Survey of Consumer Finances revealed. From 2019 to 2022, the median net worth, or wealth, for American families surged 37% — the largest jump since the Fed began keeping track — as Americans received aid from the federal government while stock and home values soared. From 2022 to 2025, Americans families' median net worth rose by a much smaller 2%, bringing it to $215,900.
